paragraphs: This passage is about the way back. A person who had to live outside the camp gets a priest who walks out to examine him (Leviticus 14:3), and a path that ends with atonement made "before the LORD" (Leviticus 14:18). God spells out the road home, step by step. Friend, that's a God who builds a road, not a wall!

Now look at the poor person. The text says to bring "whichever he can afford" (Leviticus 14:22), and the priest still makes atonement before the LORD for the one to be cleansed (Leviticus 14:31). Nobody gets turned away from this oven because of a thin wallet. If you've ever felt like you came to God with too little, this is for YOU.

Then there's the house with mildew. The owner doesn't scrape it himself or hide it. He goes to the priest and says, "Something like mildew has appeared in my house." (Leviticus 14:35). I've tried hiding a burnt batch under the cooling rack, and that cookie never un-burned. Bring it out, friend, because in the end it's God's law that tells us when something is clean (Leviticus 14:57).
